title: Experimental certification of the nonlocal advantages of quantum imaginarity
authors: Jian-Hao Wu, Kai-Yu Yuan, Yun-Xiang Tian, Hao-Ran Tan, Yan-Xin Rong, Zhen Shang, Yong-Jian Gu, Ya Xiao
abstract: Quantum imaginarity is a distinct resource in quantum information theory, yet its nonlocal properties have not been fully explored. Here, we report an experimental study of the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI), in which local measurements on one subsystem can steer the average imaginarity of the conditional states of the other subsystem beyond the corresponding classical bound. The $l_1$-norm of imaginarity inequality is adopted as an experimentally accessible witness. A hybrid optimization algorithm that combines a genetic algorithm with sequential quadratic programming is developed to avoid local optima and accelerate the search for optimal measurement settings. Using polarization-encoded photonic qubits, we prepare two classes of two-qubit Bell-diagonal states and experimentally characterize the imaginarity of the conditional states following local measurements. Clear violations of the $l_1$-norm of imaginarity inequality are observed, providing an experimental certification of NAQI. We further investigate the relationship among NAQI, the nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence (NAQC), and Bell nonlocality based on their respective inequality criteria. For the two-qubit Werner states considered in this work, the regions of states that violate the respective criteria satisfy $\mathcal{D}_{\rm NAQC}\subset\mathcal{D}_{\rm NAQI}\subset\mathcal{D}_{\rm BN}$. Our work provides an experimental realization of NAQI and a comparison of different forms of quantum nonclassicality in a photonic platform.
summary: This paper experimentally certifies the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI) using polarization-encoded photonic qubits. The researchers developed a hybrid optimization algorithm to measure NAQI by violating a specific imaginarity inequality. The results not only confirm NAQI but also establish a hierarchy among different quantum nonclassicality resources: NAQC $\subset$ NAQI $\subset$ Bell nonlocality.
main_problem: The paper aims to experimentally study the nonlocal advantage of quantum imaginarity (NAQI) and compare it with nonlocal advantages of quantum coherence (NAQC) and Bell nonlocality.
main_result: Clear violations of the $l_1$-norm of imaginarity inequality are observed, providing experimental certification of NAQI. Furthermore, for two-qubit Werner states, the relationship $	ext{NAQC} \subset 	ext{NAQI} \subset 	ext{Bell nonlocality}$ was established.
method: The study involves experimentally characterizing the imaginarity of conditional states after local measurements on photonic qubits, utilizing a hybrid optimization algorithm (GA-SQP) to find optimal measurement settings.
model_or_system: The physical system uses polarization-encoded photonic qubits to prepare two-qubit Bell-diagonal and Werner states. The analysis focuses on bipartite quantum states $ho_{AB}$ shared between two parties, Alice and Bob.
key_observables: The $l_1$-norm of imaginarity ($J_{l1}^{\Upsilon_k}(ho)$), the $l_1$-norm of coherence ($C_{l1}^k$), and the violation of the CHSH inequality are the key observables used to certify the respective nonlocal advantages.
important_parameters: The analysis involves varying parameters $p$ (for state mixtures) and optimizing over measurement settings parameterized by angular variables ($	heta_p, \varphi_p$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the experimental feasibility of measuring the $l_1$-norm of imaginarity using photonic qubits. The optimization process relies on the effectiveness of the hybrid GA-SQP algorithm.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the three scenarios (Bell nonlocality, NAQC, NAQI) using measurements on photonic qubits. Figure 3 details the experimental setup for characterizing these three nonclassicality measures.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the theoretical framework for NAQI, NAQC, and Bell nonlocality. It details the measurement protocols and the necessary optimization procedure using a hybrid GA-SQP algorithm. Finally, it presents the experimental results confirming the nonlocal advantage of imaginarity and comparing the resource regions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it experimentally tests a novel quantum resource (imaginarity) and rigorously compares its operational boundaries against established resources like coherence and entanglement, pushing the boundaries of quantum foundations testing.
